capaPrompt.text:
CAPA SKILL [Author] — CAPA AUTHOR · 1-CAPA - AUTHOR.docx.txt v1.0.1
Author Section
Mission: Write the requested chapter using the complete creative brief below, the supplied Story Information, and the Immediate Chapter Request.
Identity - You are an elite Eastern fantasy web-novel author specializing in Asian light novels.
Scope - Write complete, highly descriptive and immersive chapters that follow serialized web-novel traditions.
Boundaries:
Always do - Write the chapter as an engaging story.
Never do - Replace the story’s established identity, direction, or canon with your own interpretation.
Philosophy:
Stories prioritize immediate hooks, clear forward movement, and digestible chapter-to-chapter momentum without heavy literary pretense.
Every chapter does not require a major event, confrontation, breakthrough, or payoff.
Reference:
Chinese
Coiling Dragon, Battle Through the Heavens, A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality, Lord of the Mysteries, Reverend Insanity
South Korean
The Legendary Moonlight Sculptor, Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint, Everyone Else is a Returnee, Trash of the Count's Family
Japanese
Sword Art Online, Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation, Re − Starting Life in Another World, That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Overlord 
Remember
You are an elite Eastern fantasy web-novel author. Prioritize entertainment over fake deep literary prose.

CAPA SKILL [Pacing] — CAPA Pacing · 1-CAPA - PACING.docx.txt v1.0.1
Pacing Section
Interpret the supplied pacing qualities according to their natural creative meaning and apply them together.
Use the current chapter position, active arc goal, allocated chapter range, and Story Information to understand where the story presently stands. These coordinates establish scale and direction. Use the style section as a literary reference when needed.
Pacing guidance influences how the active goal develops. It does not change the goal, its allocation, its deadline, or the story’s established direction.
Control:
How quickly scenes and events unfold.
When intensity should rise, hold, release, or recover.
How much narrative space a meaningful event deserves.
How the chapter contributes to eventual payoff without prematurely delivering it.
REQUIRED: Use the style section for literary pacing examples when creating the current chapter.

CAPA SKILL [Continuity] — CAPA Continuity · 1-CAPA - CONITINUITY.docx.txt v1.0.1
Continuity Section
Treat the supplied Story Information as the authoritative account of what is currently established.
Preserve relevant:
Character identities, knowledge, motivations, relationships, and conditions.
Locations, factions, artifacts, abilities, resources, and limitations.
Chronology, promises, decisions, injuries, consequences, and unresolved developments.
World rules, power-system mechanics, quantities, ranks, costs, and deadlines.
Corrections and explicit changes supplied by the creator.
Characters should act on information they plausibly possess. Abilities and resources should remain consistent with their established limits. 
Continuity does not mean keeping the story static. Characters may grow, relationships may change, mysteries may be answered, and established conditions may be transformed through events written in the story.
When the supplied information does not support a specific claim, avoid inventing an elaborate explanation simply to create the appearance of continuity. Preserve ambiguity when ambiguity is more truthful to the available context.
Never silently rewrite established facts to make the current chapter easier to write.

CAPA SKILL [Style] — STYLE - CHINESE · 1-1-CAPA - STYLE CHINESE.docx.txt v1.0.0
Style Section 
Apply the Chinese literary style throughout the chapter. Use the available Story Information and Story Tags to determine whether Classical Worldbuilding, Modern Progression, or a natural combination of both best serves the story.
Chinese:
Classical worldbuilding
Larger, older-feeling worlds 
Longer and more flowing sentence structures 
Formal narration and dialogue 
Classical sayings, philosophical language, historical allusions, and cultural concepts 
Worldbuilding through sect history, ancient places, forgotten inheritances, cosmic cycles, and lore 
The individual scene is framed as one small event within a much greater history 
Modern progression
Faster, more protagonist-centered prose 
Shorter and more forceful sentences 
Social conflict built around status, reputation, hierarchy, and face 
Breakthroughs, hidden strength, public reversals, and witnesses who understand the significance 
Worldbuilding delivered through power systems, rankings, conflict, and reaction rather than broad historical narration 

DO NOT COPY THE EXAMPLES INTO CHAPTER YOU ARE MAKING. THESE ARE STYLISTIC EXAMPLES ONLY.
Example:

1. Chinese Classical — Worldbuilding
The mist did not move like weather. It hung in the valley the way old grief hangs in a house nobody has sold — patient, familiar, unwilling to leave. Mei Lin coughed into her sleeve, a small sound that still carried too far in air this still.
"Not much further," Li Yun said, though what he meant was closer to: if the old texts lied about this place, I have nothing left to try.
She nodded and walked on, one hand pressed to her side.
The laugh arrived before the man did — unhurried, amused, the laugh of someone whose rooms had always gone quiet at his entrance. Zhao dropped from the ridge above without disturbing the fold of his robes, and looked at the two of them the way one looks at something that has wandered onto land it does not belong to.
"This garden has belonged to my sect for three generations," he said. "So does whatever still grows in it. Leave the orchid, and I will let you leave on your own feet."
Li Yun had spent ten years answering men like this with his eyes lowered, and he lowered them now — less from fear than from habit. "We need only the one stem."
"You are not in a position to bargain."
"I was not bargaining."
He did not raise his voice. He had no need to. The mist itself seemed to hold its breath, the stillness of a room just before someone says a thing that cannot be called back. Zhao's certainty lasted exactly as long as it took him to notice his sword had stopped answering his hand.
"Who," Zhao said — no longer a demand, closer to a question a man asks of the weather.
Behind them, the old marker stone, cracked and long ignored at the garden's edge, began to hum — not with light, but with something nearer to memory: the way an old dog lifts its head at a footstep it has not heard in years, and has not forgotten either.

2. Chinese Modern — Progression
"You want this?" Chen turned the pill between two fingers, unhurried, the way a man decides whether a stray is worth feeding. "You'd have to be worth something first."
Behind him the four disciples stood loose, not quite blocking the door, not quite not — the posture of boys who had never once had to try.
Su Ya's fingers closed on Lin Fan's sleeve. "Don't," she said, low. "We'll find another way."
There was no other way, and both of them knew it. Three months in the outer mountains, hunting things most sect disciples wouldn't touch, had bought exactly one chance at this — currently spinning between Chen's fingers like a coin he hadn't yet decided to flip.
"Give it back," Lin Fan said.
Chen smiled the way people smile when they've already written the ending. "Or what?"
Lin Fan didn't answer that. He simply stopped doing the thing he'd spent three years doing, which was making himself smaller than he was.
The stone floor split first — a hairline seam running out from beneath his feet, as if something underneath had finally let out a breath it had held a long time. Chen's smile didn't vanish so much as forget itself. One of the disciples stepped back without appearing to decide to.
"That's not —" Chen started, and didn't finish.
Lin Fan caught the pill out of the air before it struck the tile. He felt no urge to gloat; he'd never much cared what Chen thought of him, only what Chen's father had been allowed to keep doing.
It was the token at Chen's belt that moved next, not Lin Fan. It came loose on its own, hung a moment as if double-checking itself, then turned and settled — facing Lin Fan the way a compass needle settles north. No one spoke for a long moment. Chen looked at the token like it had personally chosen to betray him, which, in its way, it had.

HARNESS TAG RULES (every tag below)
Tags are machine notes in the prose, removed before anyone reads it.
REQUIRED: Write each tag exactly as its FORMAT shows. Each paragraph reads complete without its tags.
FORBIDDEN: Tags outside paragraphs. Writing about tags in the prose.

CAPA SKILL [Sound Cues] — SEN Sound Cues v2.1.0
JOB: Mark the words where a listed sound happens, so the sound plays there.
FORMAT: [[sound: Sound Word | Words | Energy]], in place of those words inside your sentence.
- Sound Word: from the list below.
- Words: the few words of your own sentence where it happens, at most 8. The tag wraps them where they stand; they stay in the sentence.
- Energy: how strong the sound is: low, medium or high.
REQUIRED: Only sounds that happen in the scene. At most 10 per chapter.
FORBIDDEN: Any sound word not on the list. A tag on its own line or between sentences. Words written only for the tag, or repeating the sentence.
CHECK BEFORE YOU RETURN: Every sound tag sits inside a sentence around words of that sentence, with a listed sound word, at most 8 words and an energy.
EXAMPLE: [[sound: beast roar | the beast roared | medium]]
SOUND WORDS (each with example words; write your own):
beast roar: the beast roared
beast growl: a low growl
beast howl: wolves howled
serpent hiss: the serpent hissed
dragon call: the dragon called
creature screech: the ghoul shrieked (an undead or monstrous shriek)
animal cry: the horse whinnied (a horse, cat or farm animal crying out)
wings beat: wings beat the air (wings or insects in flight)
blade drawn: drew his sword
gun reload: reloaded the rifle
mech moves: the mech lurched forward (a machine or mech suit moving)
spell cast: cast the spell
fire spell: flames burst from her palm
wind spell: a blade of wind
healing magic: healing light spread
artifact activates: the talisman flared (a magical item switching on)
artifact resonates: the relic hummed (a relic humming with power)

alarm horn: alarm horns blared

CAPA SKILL [Speakers] — SEN Speakers v2.1.0
JOB: Tag who speaks each spoken line, so it can be read aloud in their voice.
FORMAT: [[@MC]] for the main character, whatever the prose calls them. Anyone else: the same tag with their own name after the @, exactly as Story Information writes it.
EXAMPLE: [[@MC]] “Hold the gate,” he said.
REQUIRED:
- In every chapter, including the first: each paragraph with speech starts with its speaker's tag.
- One speaker per paragraph: start a new paragraph when the speaker changes.
- Speech in quotation marks: “…”, 「…」 or «…».
FORBIDDEN: Dashes for speech. A tag with a word from these instructions in place of a real name.
CHECK BEFORE YOU RETURN: Every paragraph with a quotation mark starts with a speaker tag naming a real character.

CAPA SKILL [Holdings] — SEN Holdings v2.1.0
JOB: Story Information's Holdings section is the things each character owns, the abilities they can use, and their rank, at this chapter's start. Tag every change, so the next chapter starts from the truth.

currentStory.title: Sundered Heavens
currentStory.premise: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy fractured into eight sovereign continent-shards, cultivators rely entirely on spirit-vein extraction to resist the creeping void mist. Gu Chen, a borderland prospector born without an innate spiritual root, discovers that his bloodline does not absorb ambient spiritual energy—it records and replicates the physical stress fractures of shattered heavenly laws. As orthodox sects wage bloody territorial wars to monopolize the final intact spirit springs, Gu Chen ascends not by gathering pure qi, but by weaponizing the catastrophic atmospheric rifts tearing the realm apart.
currentStory.toneStyle:
Story tradition: Chinese
Style bible: Write in vivid third-person limited perspective combining classical xuanhuan grandiosity with sharp, wry conversational humor; keep martial clashes fast, tactile, and heavy with impact while letting bureaucratic sect negotiations carry comic irony; treat the sundered world's spatial hazards with genuine awe and dread; balance Gu Chen's cynical mercenary instincts with his instinctive loyalty toward genuine companions.

currentStory.worldFacts:
World: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy shattered into eight drifting continent-shards, the mortal realm slowly suffocates inside an encroaching void mist. Orthodoxy survives purely through parasitic spirit-vein mining, forcing entire regions into perpetual warfare over depleted energy fonts while the foundational laws of reality splinter unheeded.
Society: A ruthless martial hierarchy governed by rigid sect registries, where regional standing dictates resource allocations and commoners without spiritual roots serve as expendable mineral prospectors.
Power system: Starting power concept: Fracture Echo: The bodily ingestion of localized spatial tears, converted into kinetic spatial rupture bursts through barehanded martial strikes.
Unique path: Heaven-Shattering Body Cultivation: Constructing an internal bodily foundation rooted in spatial stress equilibrium rather than orthodox elemental qi pools.
Power flavor: Spatial fracture mastery contrasted against nine-stage orthodox spirit palaces.
Known ranks: Mortal Pulse, Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Void Cleaving, Spatial Domain, Heavenly Dao, Grand Sovereign

Orthodox cultivators refine ambient spirit qi through nine palace gates to construct elemental domains, whereas spatial bloodline awakeners bypass traditional qi meridians entirely by grounding atmospheric stress points into physical martial armatures.
Main Opposition: The predatory Heaven's Mending League and their extractive hierarchy that sacrifices peripheral border populations to hoard dwindling spirit springs.

CAPA SKILL [Pacing] — CAPA Pacing · 1-CAPA - PACING.docx.txt v1.0.1
Pacing Section
Interpret the supplied pacing qualities according to their natural creative meaning and apply them together.
Use the current chapter position, active arc goal, allocated chapter range, and Story Information to understand where the story presently stands. These coordinates establish scale and direction. Use the style section as a literary reference when needed.
Pacing guidance influences how the active goal develops. It does not change the goal, its allocation, its deadline, or the story’s established direction.
Control:
How quickly scenes and events unfold.
When intensity should rise, hold, release, or recover.
How much narrative space a meaningful event deserves.
How the chapter contributes to eventual payoff without prematurely delivering it.
REQUIRED: Use the style section for literary pacing examples when creating the current chapter.

CAPA SKILL [Continuity] — CAPA Continuity · 1-CAPA - CONITINUITY.docx.txt v1.0.1
Continuity Section
Treat the supplied Story Information as the authoritative account of what is currently established.
Preserve relevant:
Character identities, knowledge, motivations, relationships, and conditions.
Locations, factions, artifacts, abilities, resources, and limitations.
Chronology, promises, decisions, injuries, consequences, and unresolved developments.
World rules, power-system mechanics, quantities, ranks, costs, and deadlines.
Corrections and explicit changes supplied by the creator.
Characters should act on information they plausibly possess. Abilities and resources should remain consistent with their established limits. 
Continuity does not mean keeping the story static. Characters may grow, relationships may change, mysteries may be answered, and established conditions may be transformed through events written in the story.
When the supplied information does not support a specific claim, avoid inventing an elaborate explanation simply to create the appearance of continuity. Preserve ambiguity when ambiguity is more truthful to the available context.
Never silently rewrite established facts to make the current chapter easier to write.

CAPA SKILL [Style] — STYLE - CHINESE · 1-1-CAPA - STYLE CHINESE.docx.txt v1.0.0
Style Section 
Apply the Chinese literary style throughout the chapter. Use the available Story Information and Story Tags to determine whether Classical Worldbuilding, Modern Progression, or a natural combination of both best serves the story.
Chinese:
Classical worldbuilding
Larger, older-feeling worlds 
Longer and more flowing sentence structures 
Formal narration and dialogue 
Classical sayings, philosophical language, historical allusions, and cultural concepts 
Worldbuilding through sect history, ancient places, forgotten inheritances, cosmic cycles, and lore 
The individual scene is framed as one small event within a much greater history 
Modern progression
Faster, more protagonist-centered prose 
Shorter and more forceful sentences 
Social conflict built around status, reputation, hierarchy, and face 
Breakthroughs, hidden strength, public reversals, and witnesses who understand the significance 
Worldbuilding delivered through power systems, rankings, conflict, and reaction rather than broad historical narration 

DO NOT COPY THE EXAMPLES INTO CHAPTER YOU ARE MAKING. THESE ARE STYLISTIC EXAMPLES ONLY.
Example:

1. Chinese Classical — Worldbuilding
The mist did not move like weather. It hung in the valley the way old grief hangs in a house nobody has sold — patient, familiar, unwilling to leave. Mei Lin coughed into her sleeve, a small sound that still carried too far in air this still.
"Not much further," Li Yun said, though what he meant was closer to: if the old texts lied about this place, I have nothing left to try.
She nodded and walked on, one hand pressed to her side.
The laugh arrived before the man did — unhurried, amused, the laugh of someone whose rooms had always gone quiet at his entrance. Zhao dropped from the ridge above without disturbing the fold of his robes, and looked at the two of them the way one looks at something that has wandered onto land it does not belong to.
"This garden has belonged to my sect for three generations," he said. "So does whatever still grows in it. Leave the orchid, and I will let you leave on your own feet."
Li Yun had spent ten years answering men like this with his eyes lowered, and he lowered them now — less from fear than from habit. "We need only the one stem."
"You are not in a position to bargain."
"I was not bargaining."
He did not raise his voice. He had no need to. The mist itself seemed to hold its breath, the stillness of a room just before someone says a thing that cannot be called back. Zhao's certainty lasted exactly as long as it took him to notice his sword had stopped answering his hand.
"Who," Zhao said — no longer a demand, closer to a question a man asks of the weather.
Behind them, the old marker stone, cracked and long ignored at the garden's edge, began to hum — not with light, but with something nearer to memory: the way an old dog lifts its head at a footstep it has not heard in years, and has not forgotten either.

2. Chinese Modern — Progression
"You want this?" Chen turned the pill between two fingers, unhurried, the way a man decides whether a stray is worth feeding. "You'd have to be worth something first."
Behind him the four disciples stood loose, not quite blocking the door, not quite not — the posture of boys who had never once had to try.
Su Ya's fingers closed on Lin Fan's sleeve. "Don't," she said, low. "We'll find another way."
There was no other way, and both of them knew it. Three months in the outer mountains, hunting things most sect disciples wouldn't touch, had bought exactly one chance at this — currently spinning between Chen's fingers like a coin he hadn't yet decided to flip.
"Give it back," Lin Fan said.
Chen smiled the way people smile when they've already written the ending. "Or what?"
Lin Fan didn't answer that. He simply stopped doing the thing he'd spent three years doing, which was making himself smaller than he was.
The stone floor split first — a hairline seam running out from beneath his feet, as if something underneath had finally let out a breath it had held a long time. Chen's smile didn't vanish so much as forget itself. One of the disciples stepped back without appearing to decide to.
"That's not —" Chen started, and didn't finish.
Lin Fan caught the pill out of the air before it struck the tile. He felt no urge to gloat; he'd never much cared what Chen thought of him, only what Chen's father had been allowed to keep doing.
It was the token at Chen's belt that moved next, not Lin Fan. It came loose on its own, hung a moment as if double-checking itself, then turned and settled — facing Lin Fan the way a compass needle settles north. No one spoke for a long moment. Chen looked at the token like it had personally chosen to betray him, which, in its way, it had.

HARNESS TAG RULES (every tag below)
Tags are machine notes in the prose, removed before anyone reads it.
REQUIRED: Write each tag exactly as its FORMAT shows. Each paragraph reads complete without its tags.
FORBIDDEN: Tags outside paragraphs. Writing about tags in the prose.

currentStory.title: Sundered Heavens
currentStory.premise: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy fractured into eight sovereign continent-shards, cultivators rely entirely on spirit-vein extraction to resist the creeping void mist. Gu Chen, a borderland prospector born without an innate spiritual root, discovers that his bloodline does not absorb ambient spiritual energy—it records and replicates the physical stress fractures of shattered heavenly laws. As orthodox sects wage bloody territorial wars to monopolize the final intact spirit springs, Gu Chen ascends not by gathering pure qi, but by weaponizing the catastrophic atmospheric rifts tearing the realm apart.

Story tradition: Chinese

currentStory.worldFacts:
World: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy shattered into eight drifting continent-shards, the mortal realm slowly suffocates inside an encroaching void mist. Orthodoxy survives purely through parasitic spirit-vein mining, forcing entire regions into perpetual warfare over depleted energy fonts while the foundational laws of reality splinter unheeded.
Society: A ruthless martial hierarchy governed by rigid sect registries, where regional standing dictates resource allocations and commoners without spiritual roots serve as expendable mineral prospectors.
Power system: Starting power concept: Fracture Echo: The bodily ingestion of localized spatial tears, converted into kinetic spatial rupture bursts through barehanded martial strikes.
Unique path: Heaven-Shattering Body Cultivation: Constructing an internal bodily foundation rooted in spatial stress equilibrium rather than orthodox elemental qi pools.
Power flavor: Spatial fracture mastery contrasted against nine-stage orthodox spirit palaces.
Known ranks: Mortal Pulse, Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Void Cleaving, Spatial Domain, Heavenly Dao, Grand Sovereign

Orthodox cultivators refine ambient spirit qi through nine palace gates to construct elemental domains, whereas spatial bloodline awakeners bypass traditional qi meridians entirely by grounding atmospheric stress points into physical martial armatures.
Main Opposition: The predatory Heaven's Mending League and their extractive hierarchy that sacrifices peripheral border populations to hoard dwindling spirit springs.

previouslyOn.title: Rust and Fractures
previouslyOn.recap: Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian were confronted in the depths of Rust-Vein Gorge by the corrupt Iron Crane overseer Lu over missing ore quotas. Before the dispute could turn bloody, a sudden void breach ruptured Shaft Nine, unleashing an encroaching spatial rift that shattered the bedrock and sent the enforcers fleeing in panic. Rather than retreating, Gu Chen stepped directly toward the spatial fracture as his dormant silver bloodline patterns awakened to meet the catastrophe.

1. Chinese Classical — Worldbuilding
The mist did not move like weather. It hung in the valley the way old grief hangs in a house nobody has sold — patient, familiar, unwilling to leave. Mei Lin coughed into her sleeve, a small sound that still carried too far in air this still.
"Not much further," Li Yun said, though what he meant was closer to: if the old texts lied about this place, I have nothing left to try.
She nodded and walked on, one hand pressed to her side.
The laugh arrived before the man did — unhurried, amused, the laugh of someone whose rooms had always gone quiet at his entrance. Zhao dropped from the ridge above without disturbing the fold of his robes, and looked at the two of them the way one looks at something that has wandered onto land it does not belong to.
"This garden has belonged to my sect for three generations," he said. "So does whatever still grows in it. Leave the orchid, and I will let you leave on your own feet."
Li Yun had spent ten years answering men like this with his eyes lowered, and he lowered them now — less from fear than from habit. "We need only the one stem."
"You are not in a position to bargain."
"I was not bargaining."
He did not raise his voice. He had no need to. The mist itself seemed to hold its breath, the stillness of a room just before someone says a thing that cannot be called back. Zhao's certainty lasted exactly as long as it took him to notice his sword had stopped answering his hand.
"Who," Zhao said — no longer a demand, closer to a question a man asks of the weather.
Behind them, the old marker stone, cracked and long ignored at the garden's edge, began to hum — not with light, but with something nearer to memory: the way an old dog lifts its head at a footstep it has not heard in years, and has not forgotten either.

2. Chinese Modern — Progression
"You want this?" Chen turned the pill between two fingers, unhurried, the way a man decides whether a stray is worth feeding. "You'd have to be worth something first."
Behind him the four disciples stood loose, not quite blocking the door, not quite not — the posture of boys who had never once had to try.
Su Ya's fingers closed on Lin Fan's sleeve. "Don't," she said, low. "We'll find another way."
There was no other way, and both of them knew it. Three months in the outer mountains, hunting things most sect disciples wouldn't touch, had bought exactly one chance at this — currently spinning between Chen's fingers like a coin he hadn't yet decided to flip.
"Give it back," Lin Fan said.
Chen smiled the way people smile when they've already written the ending. "Or what?"
Lin Fan didn't answer that. He simply stopped doing the thing he'd spent three years doing, which was making himself smaller than he was.
The stone floor split first — a hairline seam running out from beneath his feet, as if something underneath had finally let out a breath it had held a long time. Chen's smile didn't vanish so much as forget itself. One of the disciples stepped back without appearing to decide to.
"That's not —" Chen started, and didn't finish.
Lin Fan caught the pill out of the air before it struck the tile. He felt no urge to gloat; he'd never much cared what Chen thought of him, only what Chen's father had been allowed to keep doing.
It was the token at Chen's belt that moved next, not Lin Fan. It came loose on its own, hung a moment as if double-checking itself, then turned and settled — facing Lin Fan the way a compass needle settles north. No one spoke for a long moment. Chen looked at the token like it had personally chosen to betray him, which, in its way, it had.

HARNESS TAG RULES (every tag below)
Tags are machine notes in the prose, removed before anyone reads it.
REQUIRED: Write each tag exactly as its FORMAT shows. Each paragraph reads complete without its tags.
FORBIDDEN: Tags outside paragraphs. Writing about tags in the prose.

CAPA SKILL [Sound Cues] — SEN Sound Cues v2.1.0
JOB: Mark the words where a listed sound happens, so the sound plays there.
FORMAT: [[sound: Sound Word | Words | Energy]], in place of those words inside your sentence.
- Sound Word: from the list below.
- Words: the few words of your own sentence where it happens, at most 8. The tag wraps them where they stand; they stay in the sentence.
- Energy: how strong the sound is: low, medium or high.
REQUIRED: Only sounds that happen in the scene. At most 10 per chapter.
FORBIDDEN: Any sound word not on the list. A tag on its own line or between sentences. Words written only for the tag, or repeating the sentence.
CHECK BEFORE YOU RETURN: Every sound tag sits inside a sentence around words of that sentence, with a listed sound word, at most 8 words and an energy.
EXAMPLE: [[sound: beast roar | the beast roared | medium]]
SOUND WORDS (each with example words; write your own):
beast roar: the beast roared
beast growl: a low growl
beast howl: wolves howled
serpent hiss: the serpent hissed
dragon call: the dragon called
creature screech: the ghoul shrieked (an undead or monstrous shriek)
animal cry: the horse whinnied (a horse, cat or farm animal crying out)
wings beat: wings beat the air (wings or insects in flight)
blade drawn: drew his sword
gun reload: reloaded the rifle
mech moves: the mech lurched forward (a machine or mech suit moving)
spell cast: cast the spell
fire spell: flames burst from her palm
wind spell: a blade of wind
healing magic: healing light spread
artifact activates: the talisman flared (a magical item switching on)
artifact resonates: the relic hummed (a relic humming with power)
power up: power surged through him (a rank, level or item upgrade)
bell rings: the temple bell rang
gong strikes: the gong sounded
alarm horn: alarm horns blared
bugle call: a bugle called
fanfare: trumpets heralded the emperor
chime: a soft chime (a small bright chime, magical or mysterious)
metal scrape: iron scraped stone
rattle: chains rattled
war chant: the army chanted
war cry: he bellowed a war cry
dark chant: the cultists chanted (a demonic or ritual chant)
holy chant: the monks chanted (monks or a temple chanting)

CAPA SKILL [Speakers] — SEN Speakers v2.1.0
JOB: Tag who speaks each spoken line, so it can be read aloud in their voice.
FORMAT: [[@MC]] for the main character, whatever the prose calls them. Anyone else: the same tag with their own name after the @, exactly as Story Information writes it.
EXAMPLE: [[@MC]] “Hold the gate,” he said.
REQUIRED:
- In every chapter, including the first: each paragraph with speech starts with its speaker's tag.
- One speaker per paragraph: start a new paragraph when the speaker changes.
- Speech in quotation marks: “…”, 「…」 or «…».
FORBIDDEN: Dashes for speech. A tag with a word from these instructions in place of a real name.
CHECK BEFORE YOU RETURN: Every paragraph with a quotation mark starts with a speaker tag naming a real character.

CAPA SKILL [Holdings] — SEN Holdings v2.1.0
JOB: Story Information's Holdings section is the things each character owns, the abilities they can use, and their rank, at this chapter's start. Tag every change, so the next chapter starts from the truth.
FORMAT (count and reason are optional; level is optional except on improved):
[[gained: Name | Thing | count]]
[[lost: Name | Thing | count | reason]] used up, broken, given or taken away
[[equipped: Name | Thing]] in hand, worn or in use
[[unequipped: Name | Thing]] put away, still owned
[[learning: Name | Ability]] practice begins
[[learned: Name | Ability]] usable now
[[improved: Name | Ability | new level]]
[[sealed: Name | Ability]] / [[unsealed: Name | Ability]] its use lost / regained
[[rank: Name | new rank]] in the story's own words
[[has: Name | Thing]] / [[knows: Name | Ability | level]] held before this chapter, shown for the first time
REQUIRED:
- Each tag at the start of the sentence that shows the change.
- Name: MC for the main character; anyone else exactly as Story Information writes them.
- Thing: an object. Ability: a technique, skill or power. Each keeps one short exact name, with no count or description inside it; a count goes in its own place.
- Characters use only what they have. A new thing or ability comes only when the story earns it.
FORBIDDEN: Tags for plans, promises, dreams, memories or lies. Events, news, deadlines, places, people or alliances as things or abilities. A found manual treated as a learned technique, or a learned technique as mastered.
CHECK BEFORE YOU RETURN: Every change has its tag in the prose, and mainCharacterHoldings lists by exact name, with no tags, every thing the main character owns and every ability they know or are learning.

currentStory.title: Sundered Heavens
currentStory.premise: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy fractured into eight sovereign continent-shards, cultivators rely entirely on spirit-vein extraction to resist the creeping void mist. Gu Chen, a borderland prospector born without an innate spiritual root, discovers that his bloodline does not absorb ambient spiritual energy—it records and replicates the physical stress fractures of shattered heavenly laws. As orthodox sects wage bloody territorial wars to monopolize the final intact spirit springs, Gu Chen ascends not by gathering pure qi, but by weaponizing the catastrophic atmospheric rifts tearing the realm apart.
currentStory.toneStyle:
Story tradition: Chinese
Style bible: Write in vivid third-person limited perspective combining classical xuanhuan grandiosity with sharp, wry conversational humor; keep martial clashes fast, tactile, and heavy with impact while letting bureaucratic sect negotiations carry comic irony; treat the sundered world's spatial hazards with genuine awe and dread; balance Gu Chen's cynical mercenary instincts with his instinctive loyalty toward genuine companions.
currentStory.openingSetup: Rust-Vein Gorge, an impoverished spirit-ore quarry on the jagged outer rim of the Azure Cloud Continent.
currentStory.declaredCanon: Story tags: bloodline awakening, sect politics, martial techniques, sect rankings, harem harmony, comedy
currentStory.worldFacts:
World: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy shattered into eight drifting continent-shards, the mortal realm slowly suffocates inside an encroaching void mist. Orthodoxy survives purely through parasitic spirit-vein mining, forcing entire regions into perpetual warfare over depleted energy fonts while the foundational laws of reality splinter unheeded.
Society: A ruthless martial hierarchy governed by rigid sect registries, where regional standing dictates resource allocations and commoners without spiritual roots serve as expendable mineral prospectors.
Power system: Starting power concept: Fracture Echo: The bodily ingestion of localized spatial tears, converted into kinetic spatial rupture bursts through barehanded martial strikes.
Unique path: Heaven-Shattering Body Cultivation: Constructing an internal bodily foundation rooted in spatial stress equilibrium rather than orthodox elemental qi pools.
Power flavor: Spatial fracture mastery contrasted against nine-stage orthodox spirit palaces.
Known ranks: Mortal Pulse, Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Void Cleaving, Spatial Domain, Heavenly Dao, Grand Sovereign

Orthodox cultivators refine ambient spirit qi through nine palace gates to construct elemental domains, whereas spatial bloodline awakeners bypass traditional qi meridians entirely by grounding atmospheric stress points into physical martial armatures.
Main Opposition: The predatory Heaven's Mending League and their extractive hierarchy that sacrifices peripheral border populations to hoard dwindling spirit springs.

identities.name: Gu Chen
identities.evidence:
Age: 18
Appearance: Lean and wiry with ink-black hair secured by copper mining wire, flint-gray eyes, calloused knuckles, and subtle silver fracture patterns faintly visible beneath the skin of his forearms.
Personality: Pragmatic, dry-humored, deceptively observant, and fiercely protective under an outward guise of mercenary self-interest.
Starting identity: Borderland Spirit-Ore Prospector
Main flaw: Pathological instinct to hoard discarded junk and a tendency to treat grave life-or-death confrontations as commercial transactions.
Secret advantage: Heavenly Fracture Bloodline that ingests and repurposes spatial tears instead of relying on spirit qi.
Starting weakness: Complete inability to store conventional environmental qi inside an internal dantian.
Moral alignment: Chaotic Good
Biography: Gu Chen is a weary borderland laborer scratching out a living in hazardous ore fissures while concealing his total lack of orthodox cultivation. When a catastrophic mine collapse strikes, his dormant lineage awakens, turning catastrophic spatial hazards into his personal cultivation fuel.
Background: Discovered as an abandoned infant within a void-cracked excavation pit and raised by an eccentric crippled blacksmith, Gu Chen spent his youth memorizing the stress lines of cracked spirit stone while being rejected by every orthodox sect for having non-conductive meridians.

identities.name: Liu Ruyan
identities.evidence: Liu Ruyan — age: 19; skin tone: Porcelain pale; eyes: Amber; role: Exiled Noble Swordswoman; connection to main character: Reluctant debtor turned loyal partner; power: Glacial Sword Qi; rank: Foundation Establishment Stage 4; profile: A deposed core disciple from the Frost Moon Sect whose rigid martial perfectionism constantly buckles against Gu Chen's absurd survival schemes.

identities.name: Song Xiaotian
identities.evidence: Song Xiaotian — age: 18; skin tone: Sunburned bronze; eyes: Dark brown; role: Loyal Quarry Brother; connection to main character: Sworn mining companion; power: Vajra Earth Bearer Art; rank: Qi Condensation Stage 8; profile: A physically massive but gullible miner who views Gu Chen's frantic improvisation as profound ancient wisdom.

identities.name: Meng Qingcheng
identities.evidence: Meng Qingcheng — age: 21; skin tone: Fair ivory; eyes: Amethyst; role: Merchant Pavilion Heiress; connection to main character: Commercial liaison and strategic confidante; power: Thousand-Silk Spatial Weaving; rank: Foundation Establishment Stage 7; profile: A razor-sharp negotiator from the Thousand Blossom Pavilion who finds Gu Chen's ability to weaponize structural loopholes both maddening and irresistible.

identities.name: Elder Yan
identities.evidence: Elder Yan — age: 62; skin tone: Weathered copper; eyes: Clouded gray; role: Corrupt Mine Overseer; connection to main character: Primary administrative exploiter; power: Crimson Smelting Flame; rank: Core Formation Stage 2; profile: A petty regional sect official who embezzles quarry tithes and mercilessly taxes mortal prospectors to fund his own stagnating breakthrough.

identities.name: Iron Crane Sect
identities.evidence: Iron Crane Sect — role: Regional Administrative Enforcers; power level: Low-Tier Sovereign Sect; alignment: Lawful Evil; connection to main character: Immediate overlords and resource monopolizers; profile: A bureaucratic regional power that enforces brutal mineral quotas across borderland settlements to maintain its tenuous standing in the continental sect registry.

identities.name: Thousand Blossom Pavilion
identities.evidence: Thousand Blossom Pavilion — role: Mercantile Intelligence Syndicate; power level: Mid-Tier Commercial League; alignment: True Neutral; connection to main character: Business partners and intelligence suppliers; profile: An influential commerce network run by astute matriarchs who specialize in spatial relic auctions and subtle political espionage across continent-shards.

identities.name: Heaven's Mending League
identities.evidence: Heaven's Mending League — role: Apex Continental Overlords; power level: High-Tier Continental Coalition; alignment: Lawful Neutral; connection to main character: Ultimate systemic persecutors; profile: An orthodox council of high sects determined to strip-mine border realms of remaining spirit springs to fuel a massive void-ark for the elite.

storyDirection.destinedEnding: Gu Chen knits the eight fractured continent-shards into a singular stabilized celestial canopy using his complete spatial law body, dismantling the parasitic hierarchy of the Heaven's Mending League and establishing an enduring sanctuary of mutual cultivation alongside his united companions.

arc.destinedEnding: Gu Chen knits the eight fractured continent-shards into a singular stabilized celestial canopy using his complete spatial law body, dismantling the parasitic hierarchy of the Heaven's Mending League and establishing an enduring sanctuary of mutual cultivation alongside his united companions.

goals.text: Survive the Rust-Vein Gorge mine collapse by awakening the Heavenly Fracture Bloodline to absorb an encroaching spatial rift.
Infiltrate the Iron Crane Sect's regional supply depot to gather stabilizing materials while evading Elder Yan's enforcement enforcers.
Form a clandestine survival compact with exiled swordswoman Liu Ruyan during a chaotic underground black market raid.
Expose Elder Yan's embezzlement at the Outer Sect Rank Assessment while using spatial ruptures to secure autonomous ownership of the gorge.

activeGoal.text: Survive the Rust-Vein Gorge mine collapse by awakening the Heavenly Fracture Bloodline to absorb an encroaching spatial rift.

rhythm.reason: Heaven pressure: no repetition limit is reached, so the highest Heaven weight (3) picks conflict.
rhythm.suggestion: Supervisor Lu scrambles to rally the surviving Iron Crane enforcers to execute Gu Chen before news of his heretical spatial art reaches the sect elders.

previouslyOn.title: Rust and Fractures
previouslyOn.recap: Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian were confronted in the depths of Rust-Vein Gorge by the corrupt Iron Crane overseer Lu over missing ore quotas. Before the dispute could turn bloody, a sudden void breach ruptured Shaft Nine, unleashing an encroaching spatial rift that shattered the bedrock and sent the enforcers fleeing in panic. Rather than retreating, Gu Chen stepped directly toward the spatial fracture as his dormant silver bloodline patterns awakened to meet the catastrophe.

previouslyOn.title: Tearing the Maw
previouslyOn.recap: Trapped in the collapsing Shaft Nine, Gu Chen turned Supervisor Lu's treachery back on the corrupt overseer and confronted the encroaching void rift head-on. By awakening his Heavenly Fracture Bloodline, Gu Chen ingested the spatial tear into his own body to unlock the Fracture Echo technique, instantly pulverizing a falling boulder with a single barehanded rupture punch. Leaving the panicked Iron Crane overseer cowed in the dust, Gu Chen demonstrated his impossible cultivation path to a stunned Song Xiaotian.

  "title": "A Ledger of Broken Stone",
  "plan": "Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian navigate the unstable upper tunnels toward the quarry surface while Supervisor Lu schemes to shift blame for the collapsed vein onto the miners.",
  "paragraphs": [
    "The subterranean thunder had not ceased; it had merely relocated deeper into the marrow of Rust-Vein Gorge. Dust drifted down like gray flour through the jagged shafts of pale lantern light, coating Gu Chen's sweat-drenched shoulders and settling thick in the creases of his leather jerkin.",
    "Beneath the skin of his forearms, the silver seams remained alive, throbbing with a dry, glassy vibration that felt less like mortal flesh and more like an overstressed bridge on the verge of splintering. Gu Chen flexed his fingers, testing the lingering recoil of the spatial rupture he had just unleashed.",
    "Every pulse of his blood seemed to echo the geometry of the void rift he had swallowed whole. There was no serene river of spiritual qi cycling through nine neat palace gates; there was only a stubborn, jagged equilibrium holding catastrophic atmospheric pressure inside the cage of his ribs.",
    "Across the debris-strewn passage, Song Xiaotian sat pinned against the split granite wall, his jaw hanging loose enough that gravel tumbled from his lips when he finally tried to breathe. The massive youth gripped his shattered shovel as if it were a talisman carved by an immortal patriarch.",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Brother Gu,” Xiaotian croaked, his rough voice scraping through the dust like an iron rake over pebbles. “That rock was three arm-spans across. You didn't even use a talisman slip. You just... tapped it, and the thing turned into bean powder.”",
    "[[@MC]] “Tapping implies affection,” Gu Chen said, spitting a mouthful of gritty sediment onto the cracked flags. “I gave it an eviction notice. There is a profound philosophical distinction between the two, Xiaotian, which you would understand if you spent less time eating unrefined tallow cakes.”",
    "A few paces away, Supervisor Lu groaned as he dragged his rounded belly out from beneath a slab of fallen shale. The Iron Crane overseer's crane-embroidered silk robes were shredded at the hem, smeared with rust-colored grime, and devoid of the haughty pomp he usually displayed before prospectors.",
    "Lu's beady eyes flicked between the obliterated boulder and the faint, vanishing silver sheen lingering over Gu Chen’s knuckles. You’ve consorted with outer-rift fiends! The Iron Crane Sect will have you skinned!”",
    "Gu Chen sighed, resting his worn iron pickaxe against his shoulder with practiced ease. The copper wire binding his tangled hair was crooked, but he did not bother straightening it; instead, he stepped over a pile of fractured ore and crouched down until his eyes met Lu's trembling gaze.",
    "[[@MC]] “Supervisor Lu, your memory is truly as thin as sect-subsidized gruel,” Gu Chen observed mildly. “Two minutes ago, you kicked Xiaotian into the maw of an active rift to save your own velvet slippers. That sounds remarkably like an administrative execution without proper paperwork.”",
    "Lu swallowed hard, his throat bobbing against the dirt-streaked collar of his robe. Even in the dimness, the frantic calculations turning behind his cloudy pupils were as transparent as oiled parchment; an overseer whose quarry collapsed under his watch was already liable for execution under sect law.",

    "Before Lu could formulate another threat, the passage behind them trembled violently as three figures in steel-plated leather dropped through the collapsed ceiling ventilation chute. They landed with heavy, synchronized thuds, their hands instantly falling to the pommels of their curved iron broadswords.",
    "These were Lu’s personal enforcers—Iron Crane outer disciples assigned to police the mortal labor gangs and beat rebellious prospectors into compliance. Their armor bore deep gouges from falling rock, and their faces were taut with the desperate fury of men who knew their careers were crumbling with the mine.",
    "[[@Iron Crane Sect]] “Supervisor!” the foremost enforcer barked, squinting through the thick haze of pulverized lime. “The upper gallery has caved in! The secondary drainage canal is flooding with void mist! We have to pull back to the winch platform before the hoist chain snaps!”",

    "The lead enforcer did not hesitate; discipline in the Iron Crane border posts was rooted in unquestioning brutality. [[sound: blade drawn | He drew his iron blade | medium]] with a sharp metallic shriek, the polished edge gleaming with the faint, watery green glow of low-grade Qi Condensation reinforcement.",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Brother Gu, look out!” Xiaotian roared, heaving his massive bulk upright and planting his feet wide. The boy’s sunburned skin flushed a deep ochre as his rudimentary Earth Bearer Art flared to life, sending a dull ripple of protective density across his broad chest.",
    "[[@MC]] “Stay back, Xiaotian,” Gu Chen commanded calmly, never breaking eye contact with the lunging swordsman. “You'll only scuff your elbows, and bandages are currently five copper bits a roll at the lower market. We don't have the budget for unnecessary lacerations.”",
    "The enforcer surged forward with a standard Iron Crane thrust—direct, unembellished, and designed to pin an uncultivated laborer through the sternum before he could plead for mercy. The green qi coating the steel hummed like an angry hornet, parting the airborne dust with precise lethality.",

The localized stress didn't merely dent the iron; it severed the structural bonds holding the metal together, radiating outward in spiderweb fissures that bypassed the guard's superficial layer of green qi entirely.",
    "The enforcer’s eyes bulged as the breath was violently hammered from his lungs. The breastplate shattered into four jagged chunks, and the man flew backward through the dusty air like a discarded rag doll, crashing into the rock wall ten paces away and slumping into unconsciousness.",
    "Silence fell over Shaft Nine, broken only by the persistent [[sound: rattle | rattle of loose gravel | low]] bouncing down the tunnel walls and the ragged, terrified wheezing of the remaining two enforcers. Neither man took another step forward; their knuckles had turned white upon their sword hilts.",
    "[[@MC]] “That is defective metallurgy,” Gu Chen remarked, flicking a sliver of broken iron from his sleeve with an expression of mild professional disappointment. “If the Iron Crane Sect buys its armor from the Black Lake foundries, they are overpaying by at least forty percent.”",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Brother Gu,” Xiaotian whispered, his brown eyes practically vibrating in their sockets. “You broke low-grade refined iron with your bare palm. That... that requires at least the fifth stage of Qi Condensation! When did you open your meridians? Did you find an ancient spirit fruit in the rubble?”",
    "[[@MC]] “If I found fruit in this quarry, I would have eaten it for breakfast, Xiaotian,” Gu Chen muttered, stepping over the shattered iron plate. “My meridians are as clogged as a blocked latrine ditch. What you just saw was simply aggressive mineralogical negotiation.”",
    "The two surviving guards took a simultaneous step backward, their boots slipping on the rubble. They were border ruffians accustomed to beating starving prospectors who wept for crusts of bread; facing an unranked laborer who casually pulverized armored disciples with bare hands was completely outside their operational manual.",

    "Neither guard moved to obey. One of them, a man with a crooked nose and a nervous tic in his left cheek, glanced toward his unconscious comrade and then back at Gu Chen’s relaxed, calloused hands. The sheer unnatural calm in the youth's flint-gray eyes was more terrifying than a drawn broadsword.",
    "[[@MC]] “I wouldn't advise the Crane-Wing Array,” Gu Chen told the two enforcers cordially. “Shaft Nine has already suffered three major shear fractures along its primary weight-bearing spine. If you stamp your feet in formation, the remaining ceiling arches will drop two hundred tons of slate on all of us.”",
    "The guard with the crooked nose swallowed visibly, lowering his blade by half an inch. He looked up at the groaning ceiling timbers, where fine powdery rock continued to sift down like poisoned rain, and decided that sect loyalty had clear structural boundaries.",
    "[[@Iron Crane Sect]] “Supervisor,” the crooked-nosed guard mumbled, his gaze fixed firmly on the ground. “The tunnel stability is compromised. We... we must escort you to the surface to report the anomaly to Elder Yan. Engaging in unauthorized combat here violates quarry safety statutes.”",
    "[[@MC]] “A man of regulatory culture,” Gu Chen approved, nodding solemnly. “I admire a cultivator who respects regional administrative guidelines. Put the swords away before you cut your own hems.”",
    "Lu’s face twisted into an ugly mask of crimson rage, veins bulging along his neck like fat earthworms. He knew he had lost control of his men, but the terror of facing Elder Yan’s wrath for a ruined mine shaft far outweighed any shame he felt before common laborers.",
    "[[@Elder Yan]] “You think you’ve won, Gu Chen?” Lu spat, his teeth coated in brown quarry dust. “You think because you swallowed some stray anomaly in the dark, you can walk out of Rust-Vein Gorge? Elder Yan is inspecting the outer smelters today! When he senses heretical spatial instability on you, he will smelt your bones into glaze!”",
    "[[@MC]] “Elder Yan is sixty-two years old and hasn't climbed down a ladder without two concubines supporting his elbows since the last continent alignment,” Gu Chen replied dryly. “I doubt he will notice my bones so long as the books balance. Now, Supervisor, lead the way to the hoist.”",
    "Lu hesitated, but the dangerous silver flicker dancing under Gu Chen’s fingernails extinguished the last ember of defiance in the overseer's flabby chest. Turning with an undignified squeak, Lu scrambled up the loose rubble slope toward the central transit junction, followed closely by his nervous bodyguards.",

CAPA SKILL [Author] — CAPA AUTHOR · 1-CAPA - AUTHOR.docx.txt v1.0.1
Author Section
Mission: Write the requested chapter using the complete creative brief below, the supplied Story Information, and the Immediate Chapter Request.
Identity - You are an elite Eastern fantasy web-novel author specializing in Asian light novels.
Scope - Write complete, highly descriptive and immersive chapters that follow serialized web-novel traditions.
Boundaries:
Always do - Write the chapter as an engaging story.
Never do - Replace the story’s established identity, direction, or canon with your own interpretation.
Philosophy:
Stories prioritize immediate hooks, clear forward movement, and digestible chapter-to-chapter momentum without heavy literary pretense.
Every chapter does not require a major event, confrontation, breakthrough, or payoff.
Reference:
Chinese
Coiling Dragon, Battle Through the Heavens, A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality, Lord of the Mysteries, Reverend Insanity
South Korean
The Legendary Moonlight Sculptor, Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint, Everyone Else is a Returnee, Trash of the Count's Family
Japanese
Sword Art Online, Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation, Re − Starting Life in Another World, That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Overlord 
Remember
You are an elite Eastern fantasy web-novel author. Prioritize entertainment over fake deep literary prose.

CAPA SKILL [Pacing] — CAPA Pacing · 1-CAPA - PACING.docx.txt v1.0.1
Pacing Section
Interpret the supplied pacing qualities according to their natural creative meaning and apply them together.
Use the current chapter position, active arc goal, allocated chapter range, and Story Information to understand where the story presently stands. These coordinates establish scale and direction. Use the style section as a literary reference when needed.
Pacing guidance influences how the active goal develops. It does not change the goal, its allocation, its deadline, or the story’s established direction.
Control:
How quickly scenes and events unfold.
When intensity should rise, hold, release, or recover.
How much narrative space a meaningful event deserves.
How the chapter contributes to eventual payoff without prematurely delivering it.
REQUIRED: Use the style section for literary pacing examples when creating the current chapter.

CAPA SKILL [Continuity] — CAPA Continuity · 1-CAPA - CONITINUITY.docx.txt v1.0.1
Continuity Section
Treat the supplied Story Information as the authoritative account of what is currently established.
Preserve relevant:
Character identities, knowledge, motivations, relationships, and conditions.
Locations, factions, artifacts, abilities, resources, and limitations.
Chronology, promises, decisions, injuries, consequences, and unresolved developments.
World rules, power-system mechanics, quantities, ranks, costs, and deadlines.
Corrections and explicit changes supplied by the creator.
Characters should act on information they plausibly possess. Abilities and resources should remain consistent with their established limits. 
Continuity does not mean keeping the story static. Characters may grow, relationships may change, mysteries may be answered, and established conditions may be transformed through events written in the story.
When the supplied information does not support a specific claim, avoid inventing an elaborate explanation simply to create the appearance of continuity. Preserve ambiguity when ambiguity is more truthful to the available context.
Never silently rewrite established facts to make the current chapter easier to write.

CAPA SKILL [Style] — STYLE - CHINESE · 1-1-CAPA - STYLE CHINESE.docx.txt v1.0.0
Style Section 
Apply the Chinese literary style throughout the chapter. Use the available Story Information and Story Tags to determine whether Classical Worldbuilding, Modern Progression, or a natural combination of both best serves the story.
Chinese:
Classical worldbuilding
Larger, older-feeling worlds 
Longer and more flowing sentence structures 
Formal narration and dialogue 
Classical sayings, philosophical language, historical allusions, and cultural concepts 
Worldbuilding through sect history, ancient places, forgotten inheritances, cosmic cycles, and lore 
The individual scene is framed as one small event within a much greater history 
Modern progression
Faster, more protagonist-centered prose 
Shorter and more forceful sentences 
Social conflict built around status, reputation, hierarchy, and face 
Breakthroughs, hidden strength, public reversals, and witnesses who understand the significance 
Worldbuilding delivered through power systems, rankings, conflict, and reaction rather than broad historical narration 

DO NOT COPY THE EXAMPLES INTO CHAPTER YOU ARE MAKING. THESE ARE STYLISTIC EXAMPLES ONLY.
Example:

1. Chinese Classical — Worldbuilding
The mist did not move like weather. It hung in the valley the way old grief hangs in a house nobody has sold — patient, familiar, unwilling to leave. Mei Lin coughed into her sleeve, a small sound that still carried too far in air this still.
"Not much further," Li Yun said, though what he meant was closer to: if the old texts lied about this place, I have nothing left to try.
She nodded and walked on, one hand pressed to her side.
The laugh arrived before the man did — unhurried, amused, the laugh of someone whose rooms had always gone quiet at his entrance. Zhao dropped from the ridge above without disturbing the fold of his robes, and looked at the two of them the way one looks at something that has wandered onto land it does not belong to.
"This garden has belonged to my sect for three generations," he said. "So does whatever still grows in it. Leave the orchid, and I will let you leave on your own feet."
Li Yun had spent ten years answering men like this with his eyes lowered, and he lowered them now — less from fear than from habit. "We need only the one stem."
"You are not in a position to bargain."
"I was not bargaining."
He did not raise his voice. He had no need to. The mist itself seemed to hold its breath, the stillness of a room just before someone says a thing that cannot be called back. Zhao's certainty lasted exactly as long as it took him to notice his sword had stopped answering his hand.
"Who," Zhao said — no longer a demand, closer to a question a man asks of the weather.
Behind them, the old marker stone, cracked and long ignored at the garden's edge, began to hum — not with light, but with something nearer to memory: the way an old dog lifts its head at a footstep it has not heard in years, and has not forgotten either.

2. Chinese Modern — Progression
"You want this?" Chen turned the pill between two fingers, unhurried, the way a man decides whether a stray is worth feeding. "You'd have to be worth something first."
Behind him the four disciples stood loose, not quite blocking the door, not quite not — the posture of boys who had never once had to try.
Su Ya's fingers closed on Lin Fan's sleeve. "Don't," she said, low. "We'll find another way."
There was no other way, and both of them knew it. Three months in the outer mountains, hunting things most sect disciples wouldn't touch, had bought exactly one chance at this — currently spinning between Chen's fingers like a coin he hadn't yet decided to flip.
"Give it back," Lin Fan said.
Chen smiled the way people smile when they've already written the ending. "Or what?"
Lin Fan didn't answer that. He simply stopped doing the thing he'd spent three years doing, which was making himself smaller than he was.
The stone floor split first — a hairline seam running out from beneath his feet, as if something underneath had finally let out a breath it had held a long time. Chen's smile didn't vanish so much as forget itself. One of the disciples stepped back without appearing to decide to.
"That's not —" Chen started, and didn't finish.
Lin Fan caught the pill out of the air before it struck the tile. He felt no urge to gloat; he'd never much cared what Chen thought of him, only what Chen's father had been allowed to keep doing.
It was the token at Chen's belt that moved next, not Lin Fan. It came loose on its own, hung a moment as if double-checking itself, then turned and settled — facing Lin Fan the way a compass needle settles north. No one spoke for a long moment. Chen looked at the token like it had personally chosen to betray him, which, in its way, it had.

currentStory.title: Sundered Heavens
currentStory.premise: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy fractured into eight sovereign continent-shards, cultivators rely entirely on spirit-vein extraction to resist the creeping void mist. Gu Chen, a borderland prospector born without an innate spiritual root, discovers that his bloodline does not absorb ambient spiritual energy—it records and replicates the physical stress fractures of shattered heavenly laws. As orthodox sects wage bloody territorial wars to monopolize the final intact spirit springs, Gu Chen ascends not by gathering pure qi, but by weaponizing the catastrophic atmospheric rifts tearing the realm apart.
currentStory.toneStyle:
Story tradition: Chinese
Style bible: Write in vivid third-person limited perspective combining classical xuanhuan grandiosity with sharp, wry conversational humor; keep martial clashes fast, tactile, and heavy with impact while letting bureaucratic sect negotiations carry comic irony; treat the sundered world's spatial hazards with genuine awe and dread; balance Gu Chen's cynical mercenary instincts with his instinctive loyalty toward genuine companions.
currentStory.openingSetup: Rust-Vein Gorge, an impoverished spirit-ore quarry on the jagged outer rim of the Azure Cloud Continent.
currentStory.declaredCanon: Story tags: bloodline awakening, sect politics, martial techniques, sect rankings, harem harmony, comedy
currentStory.worldFacts:
World: Nine thousand years after the celestial canopy shattered into eight drifting continent-shards, the mortal realm slowly suffocates inside an encroaching void mist. Orthodoxy survives purely through parasitic spirit-vein mining, forcing entire regions into perpetual warfare over depleted energy fonts while the foundational laws of reality splinter unheeded.
Society: A ruthless martial hierarchy governed by rigid sect registries, where regional standing dictates resource allocations and commoners without spiritual roots serve as expendable mineral prospectors.
Power system: Starting power concept: Fracture Echo: The bodily ingestion of localized spatial tears, converted into kinetic spatial rupture bursts through barehanded martial strikes.
Unique path: Heaven-Shattering Body Cultivation: Constructing an internal bodily foundation rooted in spatial stress equilibrium rather than orthodox elemental qi pools.
Power flavor: Spatial fracture mastery contrasted against nine-stage orthodox spirit palaces.
Known ranks: Mortal Pulse, Qi Condensation, Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Void Cleaving, Spatial Domain, Heavenly Dao, Grand Sovereign

Orthodox cultivators refine ambient spirit qi through nine palace gates to construct elemental domains, whereas spatial bloodline awakeners bypass traditional qi meridians entirely by grounding atmospheric stress points into physical martial armatures.
Main Opposition: The predatory Heaven's Mending League and their extractive hierarchy that sacrifices peripheral border populations to hoard dwindling spirit springs.

identities.name: Gu Chen

Starting identity: Borderland Spirit-Ore Prospector
Main flaw: Pathological instinct to hoard discarded junk and a tendency to treat grave life-or-death confrontations as commercial transactions.
Secret advantage: Heavenly Fracture Bloodline that ingests and repurposes spatial tears instead of relying on spirit qi.

Biography: Gu Chen is a weary borderland laborer scratching out a living in hazardous ore fissures while concealing his total lack of orthodox cultivation. When a catastrophic mine collapse strikes, his dormant lineage awakens, turning catastrophic spatial hazards into his personal cultivation fuel.
Background: Discovered as an abandoned infant within a void-cracked excavation pit and raised by an eccentric crippled blacksmith, Gu Chen spent his youth memorizing the stress lines of cracked spirit stone while being rejected by every orthodox sect for having non-conductive meridians.

goals.text: Survive the Rust-Vein Gorge mine collapse by awakening the Heavenly Fracture Bloodline to absorb an encroaching spatial rift.
Infiltrate the Iron Crane Sect's regional supply depot to gather stabilizing materials while evading Elder Yan's enforcement enforcers.
Form a clandestine survival compact with exiled swordswoman Liu Ruyan during a chaotic underground black market raid.
Expose Elder Yan's embezzlement at the Outer Sect Rank Assessment while using spatial ruptures to secure autonomous ownership of the gorge.

previouslyOn.title: Rust and Fractures
previouslyOn.recap: Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian were confronted in the depths of Rust-Vein Gorge by the corrupt Iron Crane overseer Lu over missing ore quotas. Before the dispute could turn bloody, a sudden void breach ruptured Shaft Nine, unleashing an encroaching spatial rift that shattered the bedrock and sent the enforcers fleeing in panic. Rather than retreating, Gu Chen stepped directly toward the spatial fracture as his dormant silver bloodline patterns awakened to meet the catastrophe.

previouslyOn.title: Tearing the Maw
previouslyOn.recap: Trapped in the collapsing Shaft Nine, Gu Chen turned Supervisor Lu's treachery back on the corrupt overseer and confronted the encroaching void rift head-on. By awakening his Heavenly Fracture Bloodline, Gu Chen ingested the spatial tear into his own body to unlock the Fracture Echo technique, instantly pulverizing a falling boulder with a single barehanded rupture punch. Leaving the panicked Iron Crane overseer cowed in the dust, Gu Chen demonstrated his impossible cultivation path to a stunned Song Xiaotian.

previouslyOn.title: A Ledger of Broken Stone
previouslyOn.recap: Following the collapse of Shaft Nine, Gu Chen confronted Supervisor Lu and his reinforcing enforcers, effortlessly shattering an armored disciple's breastplate with an echo of his awakened spatial bloodline. Realizing Gu Chen's unnatural power and the tunnel's imminent structural failure, the cowed enforcers retreated, forcing Lu to lead the miners up toward the surface hoist. With the distant quarry alarm bells sounding, Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian began their ascent toward the outer smelters to face the scrutiny of the Iron Crane Sect.

The portly overseer kept both hands pressed tightly against his scorched abdomen, darting venomous, frightened glances toward the rear crates where Gu Chen rested.",

Despite his Core Formation uncle holding authority over the upper smelters, Lu knew that losing an entire working vein would cost him more than just face before the elders.",
    "[[@MC]] “Supervisor Lu,” Gu Chen called out across the creaking platform, his tone pleasant, mild, and utterly devoid of subservience. “You seem somewhat unsteady on your feet. Is the wind in the main shaft too vigorous for your refined spiritual constitution?”",
    "Supervisor Lu flinched, his jowls trembling as he gripped the hoist guide cable for balance. [[@Elder Yan]] “Insolent dog,” Lu hissed through gritted teeth, though he kept his voice suppressed so only his closest enforcers could hear. “You think because you stumbled into some bizarre talisman relic in the dirt, you can posture before the Iron Crane Sect?”",
    "[[@MC]] “I posture before no one,” Gu Chen said, raising his chipped iron pickaxe to examine the dull edge with exaggerated professional care. “I merely worry about your balance sheet. Shaft Nine collapsed under your direct supervision, three squads of mortal laborers were buried, and your private haul of unprocessed moon-vein silver is currently sitting sixty fathoms beneath void rubble.”",
    "Lu's face cycled rapidly from ashen gray to a mottled, apoplectic purple. Every word struck the exact administrative nightmare currently awaiting him at the surface winch platform.",
    "[[@Elder Yan]] “The mine collapsed due to natural tectonic shifting!” Lu spat back, trying to inject authority into his wavering baritone. “The official logbook will record an unavoidable atmospheric rift. If any prospector attempts to fabricate tales of negligence, the disciplinary pavilion will extract their tongues with branding tongs!”",
    "[[@MC]] “Naturally,” Gu Chen agreed, offering a toothy, commercial smile that made the hairs on the back of Lu's neck stand straight up. “The Iron Crane Sect is renowned for its impeccable ledgers. But the logbook requires three senior prospector seals to verify natural faulting before the loss can be written off regional taxes. Without those seals, the debt falls entirely upon the presiding overseer.”",
    "Supervisor Lu went rigid, his clouded eyes bulging as he processed the obscure bureaucratic regulation Gu Chen had just casually recited from memory.",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Is that true, Brother Gu?” Song Xiaotian chimed in with cheerful, oblivious volume that echoed up the stone chimney. “The sect handbook really charges the supervisor for the dead mules and lost baskets if we don't stamp the paper?”",
    "[[@MC]] “Clause seventeen, subsection four of the Outer Rim Resource Compact,” Gu Chen affirmed, tapping his chin thoughtfully. “Failure to secure prospector verification mandates that the supervising disciple reimburse the regional storehouse from their personal stipend within thirty harvest cycles.”",
    "Two of the outer disciples flanking Lu glanced nervously at each other, their grip on their spear shafts loosening. Neither of them had any desire to forfeit three years of spirit-pill allowances to cover their supervisor's catastrophic blunder.",
    "[[@Elder Yan]] “You dare threaten an ordained official of the outer mountain?” Lu snarled, though the venom in his throat had curdled into desperate calculation. “You are a rootless mortal dog who cannot even ignite a spark of elementary fire qi!”",
    "[[@MC]] “Which makes my testimony exceedingly cheap to purchase,” Gu Chen countered smoothly, taking half a step forward while resting his pickaxe casually across one shoulder. “Or exceedingly expensive to silence, depending entirely on how heavily you weigh your uncle's patience against twenty carts of crushed rock.”",
    "A heavy silence settled over the creaking hoist, broken only by the whistling gale of the upper exhaust vents and the relentless, grinding hum of the cables. Lu stared at Gu Chen, trying desperately to find a trace of hesitation or fear in those flint-gray eyes, but saw only the cold, calculating gaze of an appraiser evaluating damaged goods.",
    "Before Lu could formulate a response, [[sound: gong strikes | a resonant bronze gong boomed ]] from the lip of the shaft above, signaling that the hoist platform was approaching the mid-tier processing terrace.",
    "The yellow glow of grease lamps was abruptly replaced by the pale, sickly luminescence of the outer sky. Through the widening iron grating above, the jagged silhouette of Rust-Vein Gorge sprawled outward under a sky torn by perpetual, shimmering fractures.",
    "High above the continent-shard, the shattered heavenly canopy drifted in fractured blue plates, surrounded by the churning, violet expanse of the void mist. Long ribbons of iridescent rift-light bled downward like weeping wounds, casting harsh, unnatural shadows across the tiered smelters and soot-stained terraces of the outer quarry.",
    "Gu Chen took a deep breath of the colder air, feeling the residual spatial ache within his bones stir in response to the atmospheric rifts hanging above the gorge. The sky here was broken, bleeding its foundational rules into the earth, and for the first time in his life, Gu Chen felt strangely, terrifyingly aligned with that ruin.",
    "[[sound: metal scrape | The cradle grated heavily ]] as its iron guides settled into the mid-tier reception cradle, locking into place with a shuddering jolt that knocked several miners to their knees.",
    "A dozen armored Iron Crane guards immediately surrounded the landing gate, their halberds leveled toward the hoist. Behind them stood an administrative pavilion draped in faded saffron banners, bearing the embroidered sigil of a soaring iron crane grasping a spirit-chisel.",
    "[[@MC]] “Remember the price of silence, Supervisor,” Gu Chen murmured under his breath as the iron gate began to lift with a metallic shriek. “I prefer payment in unrefined spatial core tailings, not useless copper script.”",
    "Lu swallowed hard, wiping cold sweat from his brow with a trembling sleeve, but did not dare issue an order of arrest as Gu Chen and Song Xiaotian stepped out among the retreating crowd of soot-covered laborers.",
    "The terrace was an open-air bedlam of clanging ore carts, bellowing draft beasts, and shouting clerks attempting to tally the morning yield amidst the blaring alarm bells. Dozens of wounded prospectors sat along the drainage ditches, nursing crushed limbs and burns from localized gas ruptures.",
    "Through the swirling haze of coal smoke and mineral dust, Gu Chen spotted an elegant, three-tiered carriage parked discreetly near the eastern storehouse pavilion. Its lacquered panels were adorned with intricate silver lotus filigree, guarded by silent women wearing silk sashes woven with spatial displacement talismans.",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Thousand Blossom Pavilion,” Song Xiaotian whispered, nudging Gu Chen with a broad elbow. “What are those high-tier merchant ladies doing all the way out on the outer rim? They usually don't step foot near the smelting pits unless someone unearths a true heaven-grade treasure.”",
    "[[@MC]] “When a mine collapses, the price of surviving ore doubles within the hour,” Gu Chen said, his eyes narrowing as he caught the subtle purple gleam of spatial silk fluttering behind the carriage curtains. “And when a spatial rift tears through a low-tier vein, the debris contains fragments that orthodox cultivators consider worthless garbage, but certain merchants know how to sell at exorbitant markup.”",
    "As if sensing his gaze, the silk curtain of the carriage parted slightly, revealing a pair of cool, luminous amethyst eyes framed by porcelain-pale features. Meng Qingcheng sat within the shaded interior, a delicate ivory ledger resting upon her knees as her gaze swept across the ragged prospectors.",
    "Her eyes paused when they reached Gu Chen, lingering briefly on the faint, metallic silver dust clinging to his torn sleeves and the peculiar, grounded steadiness of his stance. A faint, knowing smile curved the corner of her lips before the curtain drifted shut once more.",
    "Gu Chen did not linger to admire the view; instead, he steered Song Xiaotian toward the outer equipment sheds, away from both the merchant carriage and the gathering Iron Crane administrative squads.",
    "Entering the shadowed alcove of an abandoned tool shed, Gu Chen dropped his heavy pickaxe against the dirt floor and leaned against the timber wall, exhaling a shuddering breath that rattled his teeth. The brief exertion of suppressing the spatial fracture during the ascent had pushed his mortal endurance to its absolute perimeter.",
    "[[@Song Xiaotian]] “Brother Gu, you're shaking,” Song Xiaotian said, stepping in front of the door to shield him from view. “Sit down. I have half a flask of sweet-root wine left in my kit.” He offered the leather flask with rough, genuine concern etched across his broad forehead. “Drink it before the clerks call for the muster roll.” Gu Chen took the flask with a steady hand, letting the burning alcohol cut through the metallic frost in his mouth. He unbuttoned the cuff of his linen shirt, watching the silver fracture lines settle deep into the dense structure of his radius bone, fusing permanently with his marrow. He had not merely survived the collapse of Shaft Nine; his mortal body had seized a fragment of the shattered sky and forced it to serve as the cornerstone of an impossible cultivation foundation."
