chapters.title: Ambush at the North Ridge Gate
chapters.prose:
The jagged basalt chimneys of the Whispering Rifts exhaled cold, whistling drafts that smelled of ionized ozone and powdered slag. Gu Chen paused behind a fractured boulder, tightening the crude bind of his ink-black hair with a twist of that bit sharply into his scalp. Below them, sprawling across a wide terrace carved into the obsidian cliffs, stood the low-slung, iron-plated compound of the regional supply depot.

"The southern approach is completely sealed by twin arrays of crimson fire lamps," Song Xiaotian whispered, his massive sunburned shoulders brushing against the porous cliff rock. He squinted through the gray haze, adjusting his grip on a heavy quarry spade. "Brother Gu, if we try that path, the sect's bronze bells will ring before we even smell the threshold."

"Which is precisely why we are taking the high cleft behind the water sluice," Gu Chen muttered, patting the coarse leather hanging at his waist, which held . "Yan’s ledger noted that the outer boundary array suffers a phase lag every nine breaths due to a rusted spirit conduit. A broken formation is just a locked door with a missing bolt."

A crisp gust whipped fine shale across the ledge, rustling the hem of pale silk. Liu Ruyan stepped forward, her amber eyes scanning the jagged ridgeline above the depot. The icy chill radiating from her sheath seemed to push the stagnant mountain air aside, crisp and biting.

"Do not assume regional overseers are entirely incompetent," Liu Ruyan said quietly, her voice carrying the rigid precision of an exiled core disciple. "The Iron Crane Sect may be a low-tier flock of scavengers, but they guard their winter supplies with blood hounds and crossbow lines. If Yan survived your strike, his hounds already have our scent."

Gu Chen glanced at her with a faint smirk, adjusting his coarse linen sleeves to hide the dull silver lines tracing his forearm bones. His ribs still ached from the violent clash on the smelter terrace, but within the deep marrow of his arms, the swallowed spatial turbulence thrummed with a heavy, steady pulse.

"Elder Yan is currently embedded three cubits into the hoist platform with a scorched beard and shattered ribs," Gu Chen remarked dryly. "Unless he learned to fly backward through stone, he is not leading any patrols today. His junior officers, on the other hand, have quotas to answer for. Fear makes small dogs bite wildly."

From the shadow of an overhanging crag, Meng Qingcheng drifted into view without kicking up a single pebble. Her amethyst eyes flickered over the valley floor, her fingers delicately twirling a fine thread of shimmering silver silk that vanished into the ambient mist.

"Gu Chen is right about the hounds, at least," Meng Qingcheng said, her lips curving with amused coolness. "The Thousand Blossom Pavilion’s scouts reported three squads departing the depot half an incense ago. Two went south toward the crash site. The third, however, never made it down to the gorge floor."

Gu Chen’s flint-gray eyes narrowed as he caught the sudden shift in the breeze. The wind did not merely whistle through the stone spires; it broke against unseen solid barriers stationed along the rim.

"They did not go down because they knew anyone fleeing the terrace would avoid the open roads," Gu Chen whispered, dropping his center of gravity. "Xiaotian, drop flat."

Song Xiaotian did not hesitate, throwing his bulk into the shadow of the basalt shelf. An instant later, a piercing screech tore through the thin mountain air as three iron-fletched ballista bolts shattered the stone where Gu Chen’s head had rested a heartbeat prior.

Iron scrapers ground against granite as five figures dropped from the upper crags in coordinated descent. They wore the oiled gray mail and high crane-crested helms of Iron Crane enforcement scouts, each gripping a jagged serrated falchion that gleamed with sickly green wind qi.

The scout leader, a lean cultivator with a notched scar running across his lip and cold Qi Condensation Stage 9 aura billowing around him, sneered down at the quarry workers. "A pack of runaway mole-rats and two disgraced women. Overseer Yan offered ten thousand low-grade spirit stones for the runt’s head, unbroken or crushed!"

"Disgraced?" Liu Ruyan’s amber gaze turned to solid permafrost. She drew her slender steel sword in a single, fluid arc, the frosty edge humming with Foundation Establishment chill that instantly frosted the gravel beneath her boots.

"Ten thousand?" Gu Chen let out a genuine chuckle, stepping past Liu Ruyan before she could leap forward. "I knew Yan was embezzling from the furnace tithes, but offering ten thousand for a mortal miner without a spiritual root is practically an admission of financial fraud. You should arrest him instead."

The scout leader’s eyes flashed with fury at the prospector's insolence. "Cut his limbs off and toss the tongue to the pit beasts! Formation crane-dive!"

Two scouts flanked from the left, their curved blades whistling through the air as they channeled green gale blades to hem in the group's flanks. Song Xiaotian bellowed, stepping forward to intercept them with his massive frame.

Xiaotian roared with sudden battle fury as he slammed his quarry spade directly into the stone ground. A dull, earthen yellow barrier flared to life around his thick forearms, channeling his Vajra Earth Bearer Art to catch the whistling wind blades with a resounding thud of compressed mud and iron.

"Nobody touches Brother Gu’s neck while my shoulders can still haul stone!" the burly youth shouted, gritting his teeth as the impact cracked the rocks under his calloused bare feet.

The third scout tried to vault over the barricade, but Meng Qingcheng’s fingers flicked lazily through the air. A nearly invisible snare of Thousand-Silk Spatial Weaving tightened across the empty gap, catching the scout’s armored ankles with razor precision and sending him crashing headfirst into the shale with an undignified howl.

"Careless feet do not make good fortunes," Meng Qingcheng remarked, stepping lightly to the side as her silver filaments coiled around the fallen scout’s sword arm, disarming him in a heartbeat.

That left the scout leader and his remaining flanker. The leader lunged straight for Gu Chen, confident that a mere mortal miner who relied on freakish tricks could never withstand the focused pressure of an orthodox Qi Condensation vanguard strike.

The scout leader’s falchion roared with jagged wind energy, carving a miniature vortex through the cold air aimed directly at Gu Chen’s collarbone. "Die, worm!"

Gu Chen did not retreat, nor did he search his belt for a weapon. He simply planted his front heel into a natural fault line in the stone, taking a deep, ragged breath that pulled the icy mountain drafts down into his ribcage.

Inside his arms, the dormant fractures woven into his skeletal frame flared with sharp, silvery luminescence. Where orthodox cultivators gathered qi into revolving dantian seas, Gu Chen felt only a violent, unstable shearing force—a resonance of fractured heaven echoing through his bones.

He brought his left hand up in a loose, open-palm guard, deliberately baiting the descending falchion into the narrow pocket of air just six inches from his chest.

The scout leader grinned with cruel delight, pouring every drop of his green wind qi into the blade to cleave the prospector from collar to hip. But when the steel met Gu Chen’s bare hand, there was no sound of slicing flesh.

A violent resonance cracked through him as Gu Chen unleashed the raw, jagged impulse of his internal spatial stress lines. His knuckles did not merely block the falchion; they bent the very pocket of atmosphere surrounding the descending edge.

The high-grade forged steel shivered, groaned, and then exploded into dozens of jagged fragments that showered harmlessly against the stone cliff. The scout leader’s eyes bulged with sheer, disbelieving horror as the kinetic backlash traveled straight up his sword hilt, shattering the bones in his forearm with a series of wet, rapid pops.

"Your sect buys cheap iron from the outer smelters," Gu Chen whispered, his gray eyes flashing with silver lightning. "Three parts slag, one part zinc, and zero spatial temper. You should complain to the logistics elder."

Before the scout leader could scream, Gu Chen stepped inside his guard, driving a short, heavy palm strike directly into the center of the enforcer's crane-crested breastplate. He released a Fracture Echo burst from the marrow of his right fist, sending a concussive shockwave of sheared space rippling through the heavy metal plate.

The scout leader flew backward twenty feet, crashing hard against the sheer rock face with a hollow clang before sliding into the scree, entirely unconscious, his heavy armor dented inward like a crumpled copper cup.

The fifth scout, who had been circling toward the rear to flank Meng Qingcheng, froze mid-stride, his blade trembling violently as he stared at his broken squad leader.

"Surrender or become frost on this ridge," Liu Ruyan said coldly, stepping forward with her drawn blade resting a mere finger’s width from the trembling scout’s throat.

The last man dropped his falchion instantly, dropping to his knees with both trembling hands raised high in the freezing air. "Spare me! We were only following Yan’s deputy’s orders! The depot guard is on high alert, but we were promised double wages to ambush anyone coming off the ridge!"

Gu Chen shook out his right hand, rolling his wrist to disperse the tingling residual vibration of the spatial strike. It burned slightly—his Heaven-Shattering Body Cultivation was still rough around the edges, like an unpolished iron wedge—but his bones felt denser, harder, and hungrier than before.

"Song Xiaotian, tie them to that stunted juniper with their own bootlaces," Gu Chen instructed, turning his gaze toward the lower perimeter of the depot. "Take their coin purses and whatever dried rations they have in their tunics. In this economy, waste is a spiritual sin."

Song Xiaotian grinned broadly, cracking his thick knuckles. "On it, Brother Gu! You heard him, crane-boys. Boots off, belts out!"

Meng Qingcheng walked over to the unconscious leader, prodding the dented chest plate with the embroidered toe of her satin boot. Her violet eyes lingered on the microscopic cracks radiating from the impact point.

"No spiritual root, yet you casually shatter Qi Condensation armor forged from refined dark iron," she mused, glancing up at Gu Chen with sharp fascination. "Tell me, Master Gu, which ancient void heritage did you dig out of Shaft Nine? Even our pavilion’s inner elders cannot unravel physical stress vectors with such insolent ease."

"It is called knowing where the stone is already tired," Gu Chen replied smoothly, kneeling down to search the leader’s belt. "When you spend ten years listening to quarry walls groan before they crush you, you learn that everything in this broken world is already cracked. You just have to tap the seam."

His fingers caught on a heavy bronze key stamped with the three-crane seal of the depot's inner storehouse, alongside a bundle of silk passes. A faint smile touched Gu Chen’s lips.

"Look at that," Gu Chen said, holding up the heavy bronze key so it caught the pale light filtering through the void mist. "The universe rewards thorough prospectors."

Liu Ruyan sheathed her sword with a crisp click, looking down at the supply depot nestled below the ridge. The iron rooftops gleamed under the gray canopy, surrounded by high wooden palisades reinforced with defensive runes.

"The outer guards will notice their scout squad has missed their check-in within half an incense stick," Liu Ruyan warned, her tone brisk and practical. "If the depot sounds its general muster bell, they will flood the storage yards with defensive mist."

"Then we do not give them half an incense stick," Gu Chen said, standing up and tossing the spare passes to Meng Qingcheng. "The northern rift gate sits directly adjacent to the drainage sluice. We breach the fence, grab the boundary-stabilizing cinnabar and void-tempering marrow stone, and leave before the evening watch changes."

Song Xiaotian hoisted his quarry spade onto his broad shoulder, his pockets already jingling with confiscated copper coins. "Lead the way, Brother Gu. If any more cranes try to swoop in, I’ll clip their wings with my shovel!"

Gu Chen nodded, feeling the cold, restless draft of the shattered skies brush against his skin. Every breath in this sundered realm carried the bitter reminder of a world falling apart at its seams, but for the first time in eighteen years, the cracks no longer terrified him.

Sliding Elder Yan’s spatial pouch into his tunic, Gu Chen vaulted down the basalt ridge toward the darkened perimeter of the Iron Crane supply depot, ready to pry open whatever treasures the corrupt sect kept behind iron and key.

recap.text: Approaching the Iron Crane Sect's regional supply depot via the northern ridge, Gu Chen and his companions were ambushed by an elite enforcement scout squad. Using his awakened spatial body and Fracture Echo, Gu Chen shattered the scout leader's weapons and captured an inner storehouse key. With the scouts subdued and tied up, the group prepared to breach the depot's drainage sluice perimeter before the alarm could be raised.
